tools.name: agentailor_get_blog_index
tools.description:
Returns the Agentailor blog's content map: the list of every published article with its title, date, tags, and summary.

**When to use:**
- To see what topics the blog covers before answering ("what do you have on X?").
- As a first step when you're not sure which article is relevant.
- Prefer agentailor_search_articles when the user names a topic; it returns a filtered, ranked shortlist instead of the whole map.

tools.name: agentailor_search_articles
tools.description:
Searches the Agentailor blog and returns a ranked shortlist of matching articles as JSON. One tool for all discovery: free-text, by tag, and guides-only.

**When to use:**
- "What articles cover MCP?" with query: "mcp"
- "Show me everything tagged langgraph and tools" with tags: ["langgraph", "tools"]
- "Which complete guides do you have?" with guidesOnly: true
- Combine them: query + tags + guidesOnly all narrow together.

Returns JSON: { results, total, shown, hint? }. Each result carries the article's .md URL in results[].url; pass that to agentailor_read_article to read one in full.

query.description: Free-text terms matched against title, summary, and tags. Multiple words are matched individually and ranked by how many match, so partial matches still return results. Example: "memory" or "langgraph vs llamaindex". Omit to list everything.

tags.description: Filter to articles carrying ALL of these tags (case/format-insensitive). Example: ["mcp", "security"].

guidesOnly.description: If true, return only complete guides. Default: false.

limit.description: Max results to return. Default: 20. Lower values save tokens.

response_format.description: Output verbosity. "concise" (default) returns title, url, and guide per result; "detailed" adds date, tags, and summary.

tools.name: agentailor_read_article
tools.description:
Fetches the full Markdown of a single Agentailor blog article.

**When to use:**
- The user asks a substantive question that needs the article's actual content, not just its summary.
- You found a relevant article via agentailor_search_articles and want to read it.

Pass the .md URL from the search results (e.g. https://blog.agentailor.com/posts/agent-development-roadmap.md).

url.description: The .md URL of the article, from agentailor_search_articles results. Must be a blog.agentailor.com URL.

tools.name: agentailor_list_repos
tools.description:
Lists the public open-source repositories in the agentailor GitHub org as JSON, with names, descriptions, topics, stars, and URLs.

**When to use:**
- "What open-source tools does Agentailor have?"
- "Do you have a starter/template for MCP?"
- To find a repo before reading its docs with agentailor_read_repo_doc.

Returns JSON: { repos }. Use a repo's "name" to read its docs with agentailor_read_repo_doc.

response_format.description: Output verbosity. "concise" (default) returns name, description, and url; "detailed" adds topics and stars.

tools.name: agentailor_read_repo_doc
tools.description:
Fetches a Markdown doc (the README, or a file under docs/) from a public agentailor repo.

**When to use:**
- The user asks how to use a specific repo, or about its architecture: read its README first.
- The user asks about a specific documented topic: read the matching docs/*.md file.

Only README.md and docs/*.md paths are allowed.

repo.description: Repository name, exactly as returned by agentailor_list_repos. Example: "create-mcp-server".

path.description: File to read: "README.md" or a "docs/<name>.md" path. Defaults to README.md if omitted.
